desk.headline: Q3 revenue down 10% to ₩6.28tn, operating profit down 42% to ₩250.6bn (reported 22 Oct); Q4 shipments seen up about 10%
results: The 13 November filing is LG Display's quarterly report to Korean regulators; the Q3 results themselves came out on 22 October.
Q3 revenue was ₩6.28tn, up 12% on Q2 but down 10% on a year ago as the company sold fewer mid-sized LCD panels.
Operating profit fell 42% from a year earlier to ₩250.6bn, a margin of about 4%; a stronger won and dearer chips held it back.
Net profit was ₩755.6bn, mostly from currency translation gains as the won rose late in the quarter.
OLED panels made up a record 67% of revenue, led by seasonal smartphone demand.

guidance.summary: For Q4 the company expects panel area shipments to rise about 10% on Q3 and the price per square metre to rise by a low single-digit percentage; 2026 capital spending is planned at the low ₩2tn range.

points: Rising chip, material and shipping costs, plus a stronger won, are squeezing margins.
Demand for high-end devices and IT products is soft, so mobile profit gains are expected to lag volume growth.
Large OLED panel shipments are seen at about 7.7–7.9 million in 2026, roughly 20% higher, helped by gaming monitors.
Size and timing of investment in a new OLED production method are not yet decided.
Car display demand is weak this year; a real recovery is expected only in 2027.
call.source: Q3 2026 call transcript — Earnings Whispers, 22 Oct 2026; Korea Herald, 22 Oct 2026

watch: Whether Q4 OLED shipments rise as guided despite weaker consumer demand.
Cost pressure from chips and materials, and the won exchange rate.
Debt levels: debt-to-equity was 254% at the end of Q3.
